summary: Launch readiness: turnkey onboarding (top priority), federation queries, billing, operator tooling, multi-scale participation

turnkey_onboarding.description: 100% automated city onboarding: any US city with a supported meeting platform should go from zero to fully queryable in one command. Blocking all downstream work (federation queries, billing, operator adoption).

items.name: civicclerk_pipeline_wiring
items.description: Wire CivicClerk client into fetch_meetings() in modal_ingest.py. Client exists (civicclerk.py), just needs elif branch + SUPPORTED_MEETING_SOURCES registration. Same pattern as legistar_client.
items.notes: CivicClerk uses OData API. Cities: El Cerrito, Hayward, San Pablo. ~1 session. Follow legistar_client pattern exactly.

items.name: escribe_pipeline_wiring
items.description: Wire eScribe client into fetch_meetings() in modal_ingest.py. Client exists (escribe.py), needs elif branch + SUPPORTED_MEETING_SOURCES registration. Covers Canadian cities + National City CA.
items.notes: Pipeline wiring done. eScribe sites have SSL cert chain issue with Python certifi on macOS (curl works, requests fails). Needs system cert fix or Modal testing.

items.name: html_agenda_extraction
items.description: Extract chunks from HTML agendas when PDF is unavailable. Some Legistar/Granicus cities serve agendas as HTML only — chunks=0 for these cities, breaking chunk search. Detect format and route to HTML parser.
items.notes: Currently silent failure: onboarding quality report warns chunks=0 but no remediation. Need to detect HTML vs PDF agenda format and extract text content from HTML agendas into chunks. ~1-2 sessions.

items.name: onboard_quality_gates
items.description: Strengthen onboard.py quality validation: fail-fast on zero meetings, auto-retry on transient API errors, compare ratios against baseline, and generate actionable remediation steps instead of just warnings.
items.notes: Current quality report is advisory only. Should: (1) distinguish transient errors from platform limitations, (2) suggest specific fixes per failure mode, (3) gate progression to vector indexing on minimum data thresholds. ~1 session.

items.name: issue_provider_dispatch
items.description: Generalize fetch_issues() to support multiple 311 providers (SeeClickFix, FixItMarin, QAlert, etc.) via source-type dispatch — same pattern as fetch_meetings(). Add SUPPORTED_ISSUE_SOURCES registry. Currently hardcoded to SeeClickFix.
items.notes: fetch_issues() is hardcoded to SeeClickFixClient. Needs the same config-driven dispatch pattern as meetings: load jurisdiction YAML → read issues source_type → route to correct client. Cities change 311 providers (e.g., Marin County switching to FixItMarin). YAML should specify provider, not assume SeeClickFix. ~1 session.

items.name: issue_provider_detection
items.description: Auto-detect 311/issue provider during onboarding discovery. Probe known APIs (SeeClickFix, FixItMarin, QAlert) by city/county name, write detected provider to extraction config JSON. Provider can change over time — detection is re-runnable via --detect-issues.
items.notes: detect_issue_source() probes SeeClickFix API by city name. Wired into onboard_jurisdiction() flow and --detect-issues CLI flag for re-running. Future providers (FixItMarin, QAlert) add probes after the SeeClickFix block.

items.name: onboard_transcript_auto
items.description: Auto-detect YouTube channels for meeting recordings during onboarding. Probe YouTube Data API for city council channels, add to jurisdiction YAML if found. Gated on AssemblyAI key availability.
items.notes: Many cities post recordings to YouTube. Detection could use YouTube search API by city name + 'city council'. Only enable transcription if AssemblyAI key is configured. ~1 session.

items.name: onboard_end_to_end_test
items.description: Integration test for the full onboarding pipeline: mock city with Legistar source, run onboard.py, verify all stages complete (discovery → config → fetch → store → index → quality report). Catches regressions.
items.notes: Currently no automated test for the onboarding pipeline. Manual testing catches issues but doesn't prevent regressions. Use mock Legistar API responses. ~1 session.

items.name: onboard_deploy_integration
items.description: Wire onboard.py to trigger Modal deployment after successful ingestion. Currently onboarding populates Postgres but doesn't deploy or update the live API. Should optionally deploy and verify the city is queryable.
items.notes: After onboarding, cities should be immediately queryable on the live API. Currently requires manual modal deploy. Add --deploy flag to onboard.py. ~1 session.

items.name: onboard_batch_mode
items.description: Support onboarding multiple cities in a single command. Iterate over a list of jurisdiction IDs, run discovery + ingestion for each, produce aggregate quality report. Enables rapid expansion.
items.notes: For scaling beyond one-at-a-time onboarding. Takes a file or list of jurisdiction IDs, runs them sequentially with shared config. Useful for 'onboard all Marin cities' or 'onboard all Legistar CA cities'. ~1 session.

security_fixes.description: Fix existing security vulnerabilities that undermine the trust model (Phase 0 from acceptance policy spec)

items.name: coincurve_import_hard_fail
items.description: Make coincurve ImportError a hard failure in production. Currently silently disables ALL signature verification — _schnorr_verify() returns True for any input if library missing.

items.name: require_created_at_on_writes
items.description: All relay write endpoints must require created_at and reject writes without it. Currently Optional[int] = None, omitting it skips signature verification entirely.

items.name: amlegal_client_hardening
items.description: Harden American Legal Publishing client: test parser on 2-3 more cities (LA, SF, Chicago), store Sacramento to Postgres, verify vector indexing pipeline.
items.notes: Parser tested on 4 cities. Sacramento stored (5,871 sections) + vectorized (9,224 embeddings). Turnkey onboard tested end-to-end: fixed 6 issues in modal_ingest.py, onboard.py, american_legal.py, and municipal.py for graceful handling of unsupported platforms, AMLegal cache mounting on Modal, and jurisdiction registry gaps.

observability.description: Usage logging and metrics across all deployed services

items.name: deploy_usage_rollup

acceptance_policy.description: Relay acceptance policy enforcement — attestation verification and rate limiting hardening (Phases 2-3 from spec)

items.name: http_ip_rate_limiting
items.description: Add HTTP-level per-IP rate limiting on relay before crypto verification. First line of defense against spam.

items.name: nip13_proof_of_work
items.description: Add NIP-13 proof-of-work requirement for rate-limited (free) tier writes. 20-bit target ~1s computation. Provides sybil resistance for the free tier.
items.notes: _verify_pow wired into check() as tier 3, before rate limiting. Valid PoW bypasses rate limit. Configured per event type via pow_difficulty.

items.name: relay_write_metadata_table
items.description: Create relay_write_metadata table to store acceptance_tier per write. Avoids modifying frozen Voice model. Clients can filter/weight by tier.
items.notes: Implemented as coordination_write_metadata table

items.name: attestation_proof_on_requests
items.description: Add attestation_proof field to CastVoiceRequest and other write request schemas. Currently missing — prerequisite for attestation enforcement.
items.notes: attestation_proof added to Voice model and request schemas

items.name: wire_attestation_verification
items.description: Wire existing verify_attestation_proof() into acceptance policy check on all write endpoints. Look up trusted issuer pubkey from issuer_registry table.
items.notes: _verify_attestation wired to extract jurisdiction from j-tag, look up issuer via issuer_lookup callable, then call verify_attestation_proof(). app.py lifespan provides issuer_lookup from storage.issuers. Falls through gracefully when no issuer_lookup configured.

items.name: config_driven_rate_limits
items.description: Move DEFAULT_POLICY from hardcoded module-level constant to per-jurisdiction configuration (config file or DB table). Currently every relay instance has identical rate limits and PoW difficulty regardless of jurisdiction.
items.notes: load_policy() resolves: RELAY_POLICY_FILE env var → config/relay_policies.json[jurisdiction] → file defaults → DEFAULT_POLICY. Deep merge preserves per-event-type fields. AcceptancePolicy accepts jurisdiction_id param, RelayConfig reads RELAY_JURISDICTION env var. 10 new tests.

items.name: extension_pow_generation
items.description: Add NIP-13 proof-of-work generation to browser extension for free-tier writes. Server-side PoW verification is wired but no client generates it — dead code path until this ships.
items.notes: minePoW() in civicos-client adds NIP-13 nonce tag. castVoice() and castComment() mine transparently when no attestation proof. 16-bit difficulty, ~650ms avg on desktop. Cross-verified against Python server-side _verify_pow(). Extension builds clean.

items.name: attestation_expiry
items.description: Add attestation expiry check: created_at + validity_period > now. Recommend 1-year validity. Design revocation mechanism (blocklist of revoked attestation event IDs).

items.name: extension_402_handling
items.description: Update extension to handle HTTP 402 responses from relay gracefully. Show UX guidance for attestation or payment options.

token_issuance.description: Blinded token payment system for relay writes — privacy-preserving per-action billing (Phase 4 from spec)

items.name: blind_signature_scheme_design
items.description: Design blind signature scheme using existing secp256k1 primitives. Define token format, blinding protocol, and spent-token storage.
items.notes: Schnorr blind sigs on secp256k1 via coincurve. SpentTokenStorage protocol with Postgres + InMemory impls.

items.name: token_issuance_service
items.description: Implement token issuance service (separate from relay). Accepts Stripe/Lightning payment, returns blinded tokens. Cannot link issued tokens to payment session.
items.notes: TokenIssuer class with 2-step Schnorr blind signing protocol, Wagner's attack mitigation (max 5 concurrent sessions), session expiry, batch issuance. AcceptancePolicy wired with spent_token_storage and known_token_issuers in app.py. 25 tests including full integration flow. Stripe payment verification deferred to extension_token_wallet phase.

items.name: payment_proof_on_models
items.description: Add payment_proof: Optional[dict] to Voice, Comment, CivicActionEvent, CivicCommitment, CivicCompletion models and their request schemas.
items.notes: payment_proof added to Voice model

items.name: token_verification_in_policy
items.description: Add token verification + spent-token tracking to acceptance policy. Atomic: token must be marked spent BEFORE write is persisted.

items.name: extension_token_wallet
items.description: Add token wallet to browser extension. Store blinded tokens in local-wallet.ts (already handles secp256k1). Include tokens in write requests automatically.
items.notes: Full client-side blind signature implementation: blind.ts ports blind()/unblind()/verifyToken() from Python using @noble/curves secp256k1 point arithmetic. token-wallet.ts provides persistent chrome.storage.local token storage with requestTokens() 2-step issuer protocol. Service worker handles GET_TOKEN_COUNT/REQUEST_TOKENS/SPEND_TOKEN messages. SidePanel auto-attaches payment_proof to castVoice(). Server-side: token issuer HTTP endpoints (/coordination/tokens/{info,session,sign}) added to app.py, coordination.py accepts payment_proof as alternative to attestation_proof with full token verification and double-spend check.

items.name: token_purchase_ui
items.description: Token purchase flow in extension: Stripe checkout -> blinded tokens, and (future) Lightning -> blinded tokens.

items.name: token_issuer_env_config
items.description: Make TokenIssuer deployment parameters configurable via env vars: TOKEN_ISSUER_SECRET (issuer private key), TOKEN_ISSUER_MAX_SESSIONS (Wagner's attack cap, default 5), TOKEN_ISSUER_SESSION_TTL (nonce expiry in seconds, default 300). Wire into issuer service deployment (Modal). Add to civicos-secrets. Document token endpoints and env vars.
items.source: configuration critic — flagged in sessions 2026-03-22 (token_issuance_service, extension_token_wallet)
items.notes: Complete. Modal secret 'civicos-token-issuer' created with TOKEN_ISSUER_SECRET, TOKEN_ISSUER_MAX_SESSIONS, TOKEN_ISSUER_SESSION_TTL, TOKEN_ISSUER_PUBKEYS. Wired into get_relay_secrets(). Deployed and verified: GET /coordination/tokens/info returns enabled=true with correct pubkey. Docs updated in deployment.md and relay/overview.md.

items.name: query_engine_performance
items.description: Connection pooling, vector search tuning, and end-to-end profiling for cross-jurisdiction query performance under load.
items.notes: Three wins: (1) ThreadedConnectionPool in PostgresBackend — currently opens new TCP connection per query, biggest latency source. (2) Tune ef_search from 200 to ~80 — overkill for 17k vectors, trades unnecessary recall for speed. (3) Profile cross-jurisdiction latency with 3 cities, set performance baseline. Also unifies retry logic between civicos and civicos-relay backends.

items.notes: DONE (Phase 1): CorpusProvider protocol with fetch_and_store() design. 3 providers (Meeting, Issue, Legislation). RefreshRunner.refresh_corpus() generic orchestration. 78 tests. Phase 2 (cron wiring) is tracked as cron_refresh_wiring item.

Also: live-data integration tests and RRF ranking calibration (from hardening). See docs/public/decisions/query_interface.md open questions.

Found: legislation/municipal_code timeout at 10s (what_applies takes ~40s due to external API calls). Multi-jurisdiction fan-out deferred until more cities onboarded.

federation_testbed.description: Private multi-city deployment for federation design and turnkey onboarding validation. Phase A: same-county (Marin), Phase B: cross-county (Berkeley/Alameda)

items.name: onboard_mill_valley
items.description: Run /onboard for Mill Valley (Granicus, Marin County). Document every manual step, friction point, and failure as onboarding checklist items.
items.notes: Done 2026-03-11. 56 meetings, 310 agenda items in Postgres. 7 friction points documented in docs/internal/onboarding-friction-log.md. Fixed: Granicus detection (view_id 1-5), agenda link extraction (URL pattern fallback).

items.name: onboard_san_anselmo
items.description: Run /onboard for San Anselmo (Granicus, Marin County). Second same-platform onboarding validates repeatability of the flow.
items.notes: Done 2026-03-11. 169 meetings, 337+ agenda items (extraction continuing). 28 body types. 0 new code fixes needed — Mill Valley fixes generalized. 3 pre-existing friction points remain (F1, F4, F5). Friction log updated.

items.name: deploy_marin_test_relays
items.description: Deploy 2 additional relay instances on Modal for Mill Valley and San Anselmo. Private, not public-facing. Validates multi-relay deployment.
items.notes: Same relay code, different jurisdiction config. Modal makes this cheap (serverless).

items.name: issue_test_attestations
items.description: Generate issuer keypairs for Mill Valley and San Anselmo. Register in issuer_registry. Test multi-issuer attestation verification across relays.
items.notes: Tests the issuer_lookup callable with 3 jurisdictions. Validates that attestation proofs are portable across relays.

items.name: marin_sibling_ingestion
items.description: Build a turnkey onboard-and-ingest flow, validate it by onboarding Mill Valley and San Anselmo end-to-end, then update docs so any operator can do the same.
items.source: federation testbed — data prerequisite for cross_marin_query_prototype + operator experience validation
items.notes: Done 2026-03-15. Turnkey onboard script (scripts/onboard.py) generates configs + runs Modal ingestion in one command. Mill Valley: 57 meetings, 166 agenda items, 2 decisions, 591 vectors. San Anselmo: 152 meetings, 34 new agenda items, 112 decisions, 1037 vectors. Both jurisdictions now have non-zero decisions + vectors. Chunks were 0/14 due to Granicus HTML agendas (MV) and SSL cert errors (SA) — not blocking.

items.name: turnkey_onboard_hardening
items.description: Add a validation gate (small sample + quality check before full backfill) and fix data quality gaps: HTML agenda chunk extraction for Granicus, duplicate meeting deduplication, post-onboard quality report, and idempotent re-runs.
items.source: marin_sibling_ingestion validation — gaps found during Mill Valley + San Anselmo onboarding
items.notes: Eight gaps identified: (0) No validation gate — ingests 365 days blind, should sample 30 days first, verify quality (chunks>0? decisions>0?), then scale up only if quality passes. Prevents burning $3-4 on jurisdictions with unextractable data. (1) Chunks=0 for Granicus HTML AgendaViewer sites — need to extract text from GeneratedAgendaViewer HTML pages when no PDF link exists. (2) Only 2/57 decisions for Mill Valley — thin HTML minutes, need quality signal. (3) Duplicate meetings from multi-view archives — view 2 and 3 contain same meetings, wastes LLM spend. (4) No post-onboard quality report — operator can't tell if results are good or bad. (5) County enrichment is fragile string patching on YAML. (6) No idempotency — re-run doubles LLM spend on agenda/decisions. (7) City name sensitivity — slug derivation is case/prefix sensitive. Must fix before open sourcing and before cross-jurisdiction queries can rely on this data.

items.name: cross_marin_query_prototype
items.description: Cross-jurisdiction queries within Marin County via v2 query layer. SearchRequest.include_parents/include_siblings with tier-based relevance boosting.
items.notes: Infrastructure done: jurisdiction resolution, tier boosting (self=1.0, sibling=0.8), parallel fan-out, semantic relevance scores (04792c2), noise filter MIN_RELEVANCE=0.45, 130+ tests. Data ready: SR 83 decisions, MV 60, SA 96. Decision IDs migrated to meeting-scoped ordinals (f08025f). Remaining: (1) downward resolution — query county-marin should fan out to child cities, (2) cache registry.json in memory, (3) mount v2 on REST API server.

items.description: Capture all manual steps, failures, and workarounds from Phase A onboarding. Convert to /onboard improvements and operator guide updates.

All 3 existing jurisdictions verified.

Fixed YAML generator: level passthrough (was hardcoded 'city') and self-reference filtering in parent_jurisdictions. 88/88 tests pass (83 original + 5 new robustness tests).

items.description: Ingest federal comment periods from regulations.gov API. Store as upcoming events with deadlines. Enable civic.act submission. Highest-value federal participation surface.
items.notes: regulations.gov has a well-documented REST API (api.regulations.gov). Comment periods have structured deadlines, map cleanly to civic.upcoming (type=comment_periods) and civic.act (action=submit_comment). Need: (1) API client for open comment periods, (2) store as upcoming events with deadline dates, (3) civic.act handler that formats and submits comments. UpcomingType.comment_periods enum already exists but nothing implements it. 1-2 sessions.

items.name: federal_funding_pipeline
items.description: Bulk ingest federal awards via USAspending API for all configured jurisdictions. Client exists (usaspending.py), API is free. Store in federal_awards table, add to weekly refresh, index vectors.
items.source: multi-scale participation — federal data (plan: docs/internal/federal-data-plan.md, sessions 1-2)
items.notes: Currently 5 awards totaling $17.2M for San Rafael. USAspending API supports geographic filtering, no key needed. Target: hundreds of awards across all Marin jurisdictions. Session 2: build FundingAdapter for v2 search, wire into civic.upcoming for expiring grants, add to extension.

items.name: congressional_votes
items.description: Extend CongressGovClient with vote retrieval. Store in congressional_votes table linked to legislation + elected_officials.
items.notes: DONE: CongressGovClient extended with House Clerk XML + Senate XML parsing. congressional_votes table + storage protocol. 1,491 votes ingested (173 House/Huffman, 1318 Senate/Schiff+Padilla). Added to weekly refresh.

items.name: congressional_votes_query
items.description: Wire congressional votes into v2 query layer, MCP tool, and extension. Enable 'How did my representative vote on [bill]?' queries.
items.notes: 1,491 votes in DB. Wire into v2 search (civic.search 'housing votes'), MCP get_congressional_votes tool, extension 'How They Voted' view on Federal tab. Parallels city council get_voting_record.

items.name: congressional_hearings
items.description: Ingest congressional committee hearings from Congress.gov API. Store as events, wire into civic.upcoming alongside comment periods. Federal equivalent of city council meetings.
items.notes: COMPLETE. Session 1: 421 hearings ingested (274 House, 147 Senate). Session 2: Wired into v2 search (CongressionalHearingsAdapter), upcoming verb (congressional_hearings event type), MCP tool (get_congressional_hearings), extension UX (Congressional Hearings section in pulse), and city_pulse data. All verified against live data.

items.name: local_impact_relevance
items.description: Score federal rules by local relevance. Agency-to-topic mapping, geographic text matching, CFR part matching. Extension sorts by relevance, draft_federal_comment shows local context.
items.notes: COMPLETE. Created relevance.py with 3 heuristic signals: (1) agency-to-topic mapping (24 agencies → 13 local policy areas), (2) geographic text matching (San Rafael/Marin/Bay Area/California with tiered weighting), (3) CFR title matching (14 locally relevant CFR titles). Added local_relevance_score FLOAT + relevance_reasons JSONB columns to federal_rules table. Backfilled 4,115 rules: 1,013 scored > 0 (25%). Scores auto-computed on ingest via store_federal_rules(). V2 search sorts federal comment periods by relevance. MCP tools display relevance score + reasons. Chunker includes relevance context in vector text for semantic search.

items.name: vector_llm_relevance_pipeline
items.description: Vector-first relevance pipeline: embed local policy descriptions as query vectors, retrieve candidate federal rules by similarity, LLM-confirm relevance on candidates only. Replaces heuristic-only scoring with semantic + LLM hybrid.
items.source: multi-scale participation — federal data (refinement of local_impact_relevance)
items.notes: 3-stage pipeline: (1) Define 10-15 policy area query vectors for San Rafael (can bootstrap from existing municipal_code embeddings — tested and works, 0.69 similarity for housing, 0.68 for water). (2) For each policy vector, retrieve top 30-50 most similar federal rules via pgvector cosine similarity, deduplicate across policy areas (~200-400 candidates from 4,115 total). (3) Send candidates to gpt-4o-mini in batches of 20-30 for confirmation + local_relevance_summary generation. Store score + summary. Cost: ~$0.05 for full corpus, pennies/week for new rules. Follows existing classify_topics.py batch pattern. Ongoing: new rules auto-scored on ingest after embedding. 1-2 sessions.

items.name: federal_pipeline_hardening
items.description: Fix US legislation refresh gap (only CA syncs), debug CA sync failure, close 12% embedding gap on federal_rules, verify all new corpora have scheduled refreshes.
items.notes: Done: (1) Added US federal legislation to scheduled_low_velocity_refresh loop alongside CA. (2) CA sync confirmed working (last cron success 2026-03-15). (3) Created expand_federal_rules_to_chunks() in chunker.py — adds document_type, topics, fallback text for rules without title/abstract, closing embedding gap. (4) Added 'legislation' to federal-US corpus types in index_vectors. All 8 federal corpora now have scheduled refreshes.

items.name: federal_server_deployment
items.description: Deploy country-united-states Modal server with full federal tool suite: funding search, congressional votes, hearing timeline, relevance-scored comment periods.
items.notes: Meaningful after sessions 1-9 create real federal-specific tools and data. Federal server becomes the peer that city MCPs federate with when the shared DB splits. Create civicos-federal-env Modal secret. 1 session.

items.name: state_legislative_client
items.description: Build California legislature data client using leginfo.legislature.ca.gov. Ingest committee hearing schedules, bill status with vote dates, public comment windows.
items.notes: Uses official bulk downloads from downloads.leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (same format as modal_cacode.py). Parses BILL_TBL, BILL_VERSION_TBL, BILL_HISTORY_TBL, BILL_SUMMARY_VOTE_TBL, COMMITTEE_HEARING_TBL, COMMITTEE_AGENDA_TBL. Initial ingest: 4,248 AB/SB bills + 73,721 events (hearings, votes, history). Special session bills use -x1 suffix. Daily deltas available for refresh.

items.name: state_server_deployment
items.description: Deploy state-california Modal server. Wire committee hearings, bill votes, and comment windows into the server's data. Connect extension CA tab.
items.notes: Deployed 2026-03-21. Direct URL: lounsburynw--civicos-california-mcpserver-mcp-endpoint.modal.run. 24 tools (state+federal). Fixed: Modal secret ordering (primary last), REST API register endpoint type annotation, CA legislation cron secret name. Cloudflare proxy (california.civicosproject.org) still routes to stale old deploy — needs DNS/Worker update to point to new Modal URL. Weekly cron registered (Sunday 4 AM UTC). Extension CA tab has voice/coordination support but not state-specific content rendering (acceptable for MVP).

items.name: vertical_query_tier_tuning
items.description: Tune tier weights for upward queries (city→state→federal). Parent tier is currently 1.0 (same as self), which means state/federal results compete equally with local decisions. May need level-aware weighting or separate result grouping.
items.notes: With real state/federal data, include_parents=True will return results from 3+ levels. Questions: (1) Should parent weight stay 1.0 or decrease with distance (county=0.9, state=0.7, federal=0.5)? (2) Should jurisdiction_results group by level (local/state/federal) not just jurisdiction ID? (3) How does the extension render mixed-level results? Needs real data to validate — run after federal_comment_periods. 1 session.

items.name: downward_query_scaling
items.description: Cap or paginate downward resolution for state/county-level queries. Querying state-california with include_siblings (downward) would fan out to every CA city — works with 4, breaks with hundreds.
items.notes: Options: (1) cap fan-out at N jurisdictions (e.g., 10), (2) require explicit also_include for large fan-outs, (3) aggregate mode returns counts per jurisdiction without full search. Not urgent until CA has more than ~10 cities. 1 session.

items.name: upcoming_comment_periods
items.description: Implement UpcomingType.comment_periods and UpcomingType.hearings in civic.upcoming. Surface federal comment deadlines and state hearing dates alongside local meetings.
items.notes: UpcomingType enum already has comment_periods and hearings but execute_upcoming() only handles meetings. Need adapters that query stored comment periods/hearings with deadlines. Key UX: show 'Comment period closes in 3 days' alongside 'City Council meets Tuesday'. 1 session, depends on federal_comment_periods data.

items.name: civic_act_federal_comment
items.description: civic.act handlers for federal comment drafting and submission preparation. draft_federal_comment returns structured draft guidance with rule context; prepare_federal_comment returns submission URL, deadline, and instructions. Programmatic submission not supported by regulations.gov — users submit via web form.
items.notes: regulations.gov does not support programmatic POST comment submission (ToS restriction). Implemented draft_federal_comment (AI-assisted draft with stance-aware guidance, rule context, deadline urgency) and prepare_federal_comment (structured submission context for extension UI). Both wired into civic.act via _ACTION_TO_HANDLER, registered as MCP tools in FEDERAL_TOOLS, and ref-parseable from rule:us-federal:{doc_number}.

items.name: legislation_adapter_unification
items.description: Unify legislation data path: query stored state/federal legislation first, fall back to what_applies() API calls. Currently all legislation comes via on-demand API calls regardless of what's stored.
items.notes: LegislationAdapter currently calls what_applies() which hits LegiScan/Federal Register APIs on every query. With stored state/federal data, should check storage first for faster responses and offline capability. API calls become the refresh mechanism, not the query path. 1 session.

items.name: turnkey_state_onboarding
items.description: Generalize state-level onboarding beyond hardcoded CA. Framework for adding other states (legislation source detection, bulk download client generation, server deployment).
items.notes: CA is hardcoded to leginfo.legislature.ca.gov. Other states have different legislation platforms. Deprioritized per roadmap — CA is the only state needed pre-launch. Post-launch work.
